features.name: Northern Pacific main line (as in 1883)
features.built_text: 1880 (track reached the Little Missouri in 1880; bridge under construction in Haynes 1880 photo)
features.evidence: West of the river, today's BNSF (former NP) track falls exactly on the track drawn on the 1883 plat. East of the river the plat draws the track up to ~100 m south of today's line, south of a row of blocks that today lies north of the track. Either the plat is schematic there or the line was later realigned - check NP valuation and right-of-way maps (MNHS).

features.name: Northern Pacific bridge (trestle) over the Little Missouri
features.evidence: Where the track crosses the 1883 channel traced from the plat. HAG: the train "rumbled across three hundred feet of trestle." People crossed on foot between the rails at high water (HAG).
features.sources: PLAT1883; HAG ch. I; Bismarck Weekly Tribune 1885-10-16 (an NP bridge west of Medora burned)
features.photos: mhs:91737 (under construction, 1880); mhs:95324; mhs:72459 (Huffman 1886, "Medora from railway bridge"); shsnd:00042-00151

features.name: Ford of the Little Missouri
features.evidence: "the ford a hundred yards north of the trestle" (HAG ch. I). Placed 100 yd north of the 1883 crossing.

features.name: Bad Lands Cantonment (abandoned army post)
features.removed_text: part burned early 1887; rest razed or hauled away; hospital moved to Dickinson fall 1888
features.use: army post 1879-83; ranch HQ, resort, homes and church services 1883-86
features.footprint_ft: barracks 200x22; officers' quarters 124x30; hospital 52x25 + 23x14; storehouse 100x22; laundresses 41x28; guardhouse 25x30; bakery 30x20; blacksmith 18x18; stables 54x38; ice house 30x25; two cellars 18x16
features.evidence: Eight building symbols drawn on the 1883 plat, labelled "Cantonments," NW of the river crossing. HM52: about 3/4 mile NW of Medora under the bluffs; buildings ranged round a central parade ground (Lang). Symbols are schematic, so individual buildings are not identified.
features.sources: PLAT1883; HM52 pp. 10-11 (building sizes, from post Letters Sent, 1 Jan 1880); TRC-CANT; LANG; NARA RG77 file unit 4522386 (7 building plans); SHSND MAP.032-00111 (1879 reserve map); HAG ch. I-II
features.notes: Dates conflict: established spring 1879 (TRC) vs Nov 10 1879 (HM52, HMdb); abandoned March 24 (TRC) vs March 4, 1883 (HMdb). SHSND surveyed the site with drone and magnetometry in June 2025 (PAC-MAC 2025 paper) - request the results. HAG puts it "a quarter of a mile west" of Maunders's shack; the plat puts it ~0.5 mi NW of the crossing. Cow Boy 1884-85: the buildings housed the Hyde, Hannigan, Butler, McGregor and Barker families and contractor J. A. Freeze; attached and sold by the sheriff July-Oct 1885; sold at sheriff's sale to Beckett & Foote of Dickinson 1888-89 (Dickinson Press, in HM52). BROOKS57: state highway gravel operations "destroyed the site" before 1952. A sutler's store (Frank Moore) stood on the parade ground: "long and low," with an L used as a bar and sleeping quarters behind (Huidekoper, in HM52).

Long side parallel to the track, as in Haynes's 1881 photo. Size is a placeholder.

features.name: Northern Pacific depot, Medora
features.evidence: "near today's Medora Convenience Store" (HMdb 87986). Huffman's 1886 photo (MHS 72461) shows a one-and-a-half-story board-and-batten depot with its long side along the track, a bay window for the agent facing the track, a "MEDORA" sign with mileboards, and a covered freight end; HMdb's "perpendicular to the tracks" does not fit that photo. In the 1885-86 overviews a depot-sized building and loading sheds back-project within about 15-45 m of this spot.
features.notes: "A few steps" from the Hotel de Mores (Cow Boy). Used for church services and Sunday school. Size still a placeholder (about 24 x 60 ft from the photo's proportions). MHS dates its Huffman print to 1886 but the caption says "North Dakota" (statehood 1889), so the caption at least is later; confirm the date of the negative.

features.name: Hotel de Mores (Northern Pacific Hotel from 1885)
features.built_text: 1883, as a boarding house for up to 100 (HMdb); in use by Feb 1884 (Cow Boy); brick-veneered and reopened June 1, 1885
features.use: hotel, with livery stable and bar
features.evidence: Probably building "D" of the 1885 bird's-eye view, triangulated from SHSND 00042-00071 and 00042-00195; the reprojected base agrees with both photos (5 px and 2 px), and swapping D with D2 fails that test by about 60 px. Triangulated from two or more solved photos; sight lines cross within about 1-3 m, so the position is good to roughly +/-10 m once picking error is allowed for. Why the hotel: (1) a long two-story building with evenly spaced windows on both floors, the shape of the 1883 frame hotel (SHSND 00042-00149); (2) about 60 m north-east of the depot site - "a few steps from the depot" (Fitzgerald's ad, Cow Boy 1884); (3) long side facing north (HMdb 88037: "faced north"), with its west end on Main Street, which fits the race track running to "Main street opposite the Northern Pacific hotel" (Cow Boy) and the 1885 porch on the west side; (4) gone in the c.1905 postcard - the hotel burned in 1897. Further support (Oct 16): Houghton 3013534 and 3013559 (1895) label the long brick building with a taller gabled block at one end as the Hotel de Mores; building "D" seen from the east in 00042-00071 shows exactly such a tall gable at its east end. The Historic Medora marker for the hotel stands at Main Street and Pacific Avenue, about 20 m from this point (HMdb 88037; it shares a marker cluster, so this is weak support on its own). The high 1885 view Houghton 3013473 / SHSND 00042-00193 shows a large gabled building here too. Location raised to B.
features.sources: HMdb 88037; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-02-14, 1884-04-17; HAG (Mandan Pioneer: "a large hotel") ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-10-23, 1885-02 to 1885-06-04 ; SHSND 00042-00149, 00042-00071, 00042-00195 (camera solutions, docs/photo-matching.md); Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-02-07 (Fitzgerald ad) ; Houghton 3013534, 3013559; HMdb 88037 (marker location)
features.photos: shsnd:00042-00076; shsnd:00042-00086 (1885); houghton:3013534; houghton:3013529 (interior); houghton:3013559 (1895); shsnd:00042-00149 (1883?, wood-sided) ; shsnd:00042-00071 (1885 bird's-eye, camera solved); shsnd:00042-00195 (1885-86 overview, camera solved); shsnd:00042-00194 (1885-86 overview, same camera station as -00195) ; houghton:3013534; houghton:3013559 (1895); houghton:3013473
features.notes: SHSND 00042-00149 shows a wood-sided hotel in snow in 1883 - consistent with brick veneer added in 1885. 1885 rebuild (Cow Boy, Feb-May 1885): new foundations, brick veneer by Peter Book, porches on the west and south sides, kitchen and laundry additions on the north side; lessee Arch Boyd; renamed the Northern Pacific Hotel June 4, 1885. Earlier managed by G. W. Fitzgerald. Arson attempt Oct 23, 1884. Open conflict: in the 1885-86 overviews this building reads as white or light-painted, with an outside stair at its east end, while the Cow Boy says the hotel was brick-veneered in spring 1885 and SHSND 00042-00076 shows a long brick building. Either the overviews predate the veneer, the brick read light, or the brick building is a different structure. The site falls on the block the 1957 NPS Tour map shows as De Mores Memorial Park; whether the memorial park was laid out on the old hotel site is worth checking. Facing conflict: the Historic Medora panel on site (photographed by Matt Briney, 2026) reads "located north of the railroad depot and faced west", while the HMdb transcription of the same marker reads "faced north". "Faced west" fits a front on Main Street - the west gable end of building D. Check the panel text against the marker sponsor (Historic Medora).

features.name: Roberts Hall (billiard hall and theatre)
features.use: bar and club rooms below; hall with stage, two dressing rooms above; later county offices
features.material: frame; drop siding, board paper, plastered inside
features.evidence: Possibly building "D2" of the 1885 bird's-eye view, triangulated from three photos (SHSND 00042-00071, 00042-00195 and the c.1905 postcard 00259-00003; the three sight lines agree within 0.5 degrees). Triangulated from two or more solved photos; sight lines cross within about 1-3 m, so the position is good to roughly +/-10 m once picking error is allowed for. Why Roberts Hall: two full stories about 80 ft long as scaled from the photo (the footprint uses the Cow Boy's 24 x 75) with few upper windows (a hall, not hotel rooms), a raised front on its south end, long axis north-south; still standing about 1905 (Roberts Hall stood until 1923, while the hotel burned in 1897); next to today's Old Town Hall Theater (Roberts Hall may be the "town hall" of a 1903 stereo, still to be checked); near the hotel and in view of the railroad (HMdb). Further support (Oct 16): Hagedorn's 1919 photo of "Bill Williams' saloon" (Houghton 3013539) shows a two-story frame hall with a fanlight in its front gable and a door to the upper floor; in his 1919 overview (Houghton 3013472) a dark two-story gabled building of that form, long axis north-south, stands south of the Rough Riders and north of the depot, which is where D2 is. The Roberts Hall marker (HMdb 88016) stands in a small park next to the Old Town Hall Theater, about 10 m from this point. Location raised to B; the Cow Boy's "lot 7, block 17" remains unexplained. Lot check (Oct 16): the triangulated position falls on today's lot 7 (parcel "7-8") of Block 13 - the same lot number the Cow Boy gives (Cow Boy 1884-06-26: "lot 7, block 17 ... in full view from the railroad"). Today's Block 17, in the southeast of town, is open sagebrush in the 1885 overview (SHSND 00042-00195), so the hall cannot have stood there. Either the 1883 plat numbered this block 17, or the paper misprinted 13 as 17. Neither block 13 nor block 17 is on the 1883 "Price of Lots" list (TRMF-01), so both were held back from public sale. The Historic Medora "Billings County Courthouse" panel shows a winter photo captioned "Roberts Hall housed the first county offices" (1886): a two-story front-gabled frame hall with an upper-floor door, the same form as Hagedorn's 1919 "Bill Williams' saloon".
features.sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-05-01, 1884-06-26; HMdb 88016; HAG (Medora chapter); Dickinson Press 1885-01-17 ; Houghton 3013539, 3013472; HMdb 88016 (marker location) ; TRMF-01 "Price of Lots" (Digital Horizons ndshs-dm 4191-4192) ; Historic Medora courthouse panel

features.name: J. C. Fisher's two stores
features.evidence: "two stores on Third Ave near Main St" (Cow Boy 1884-11-06).
features.notes: First planned May 1884 with Van Driesche as a three-store-room building. Tenants: Charles Cook, confectioner, and J. D. Garver, tinsmith (Nov 1884); later the Willard & Keeler meat market and Wells Fargo office (Dec 1885).

features.name: Fisher's roller rink and shooting gallery
features.built_text: planned Feb 1885; opened with a ball March 11, 1885
features.use: roller rink; church services held there 1885
features.evidence: "next to Joe's store, opposite the office of the Bad Lands Cowboy" (HAG). The Cow Boy's 1886 fire warning runs along Main Street from Mrs. Malloy's hotel to Bob Roberts's saloon (which moved into "the old skating rink" in Aug 1885), so both were on the Ferris block. Placed north of the store on Main Street.
features.sources: HAG (Medora chapter); Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-02-12, 1885-04-16; Dickinson Press 1885-03-14 ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-08, 1886-03-25
features.notes: Built by Jim Butler; opened about March 11, 1885; post office briefly inside; church services held there. From Aug 1885 it was Bob Roberts's saloon - ceiled, papered, painted, glass front (Cow Boy).

features.name: Bad Lands Cow Boy office
features.built_text: paper began Feb 1884 (masthead "Little Missouri, Medora P.O."); "Published in Medora" from Nov 1885
features.evidence: Site identified by Matt Briney (Oct 16, 2026): the small one-story frame building at 398 Main St, beside the HMdb "Bad Lands Cow Boy" marker (88045, at Main Street and 3rd Avenue, 46.9146 N, 103.5261 W). Placed there, with the long side east-west. Replaces the earlier placement inferred from Hagedorn ("opposite Fisher's rink and Joe Ferris's store"), which was about 80 m north.
features.sources: HAG; LOC sn84024777; HMdb 88045; Eaton to Sewall 1887-02-26 (TRC o292533) ; Google Street View, 398 Main St (Sep 2025)
features.photos: houghton:3013536; npshb:thro15.jpg
features.notes: Painted April 1884 (Cow Boy). The office burned on Jan 12, 1887 (HMdb 88045), so the building standing today cannot be the 1884 original; it is a later or reconstructed building on (or near) the site. Compare its form with Houghton 3013536 (Packard at the office door: one-story, front gable, side entry). A saloon stood "next door" and a frame building to rent south of it (Cow Boy 1884-04-24). Painted April 1884 (Cow Boy).

features.name: Paddock's livery stable (Medora)
features.removed_text: Paddock's buildings shipped to Dickinson by flat car, June 1887
features.material: frame; drop siding; battlement front; 2-in floor
features.evidence: "on Third St between Third Ave and Broadway" (Cow Boy 1885-02-26). Side of the street not stated; placed west side.
features.sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-02-26; Dickinson Press 1887-06-04; HAG ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-04-16, 1885-04-30, 1885-05-14
features.notes: Built by Jim Butler, finished April 16, 1885; size to be doubled (April 30). Livery office was the 1886 polling place. Paddock also moved Fitzgerald's old west-side dwelling next to his barn as Fred Banan's barber shop (May 1885).

features.name: Black Hills freight house (Medora & Black Hills Forwarding Co.)
features.built_text: sills laid July 1884; nearly finished Aug 1884
features.use: freight warehouse for the Deadwood stage and freight line
features.evidence: "on the south side of the track near the bluff... as near as possible to the butte," built "across Quick creek" (Cow Boy 1884-05-01, 05-08, 1886-05-13). Quick creek not yet identified; placed south of the track east of the depot.
features.sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-05-01, 1884-07-17; Dickinson Press 1884-07-12; Bismarck Weekly Tribune 1884-08-08; HAG ("well-built, substantial")
features.notes: Held 225 carloads; west end split into three rooms with a platform and derrick (Aug 1884); J. C. Fisher's office partitioned off inside (Sept 1884); underpinned May 1886.

features.name: Peter Book's brickyard
features.built_text: opened spring 1884; first kiln fired May 21, 1884
features.use: brickworks (10,000+ bricks a day; dark red brick)
features.evidence: "south of town where the Deadwood trail separates from the river" (Cow Boy 1884-04-24); ".9 of a mile south by river road from U.S. Highway 10 at Medora on the east bank... Section 34" (BROOKS57 p. 33). Placed in Sec. 34 about 0.9 mi south.
features.notes: Book patented a "lignite kiln" (1885). Book's house near the kiln, to be brick-veneered (1885); lime burned just west of the kiln (1885); a side-track along the bluff to the yard was planned (1885). New stockyards were built at "the brick-kiln butte" in Oct 1885 (Cow Boy).

features.name: Packing plant: main packing-house foundation
features.material: heavy timber frame on sandstone and brick foundations
features.footprint_ft: ~110-130 x 14-24 as drawn in 1956-57 (foundation remnant); NRHP gives the abattoir as 105 x 180
features.evidence: Long east-west foundation drawn about 100-125 ft south-southeast of the chimney on both 1950s NPS plans; scaled from the 1957 Tour map.
features.sources: NPS "Tour of Medora" map, Aug 1957 (NMP-TR-7008, in NPSHB 1962 p. 54, 0-600 ft scale); 1956 site plan NMP-TR 3002-A (BROOKS57 Fig. 6); NRHP 75001300; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12-04

features.name: Packing plant: ice house
features.built_text: company ice houses held 4,000 tons by Dec 1884, about 10,000 tons by Jan 1886 (Cow Boy)
features.footprint_ft: ~107 x 43 as drawn in 1957; NRHP: three ice houses 40 x 100
features.evidence: Dashed "ICE HOUSE" outline about 210 ft west-southwest of the chimney on the 1957 Tour map. NRHP says three ice houses adjoined the plant; only one is drawn.
features.sources: NPS "Tour of Medora" map, Aug 1957 (NMP-TR-7008, in NPSHB 1962 p. 54, 0-600 ft scale); 1956 site plan NMP-TR 3002-A (BROOKS57 Fig. 6); NRHP 75001300; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12-04; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12, 1886-01
features.photos: ; shsnd:00042-00071 (1885 bird's-eye, camera solved)
features.notes: 1885 photo: the plant's large building back-projects within about 15 m of this placement (docs/photo-matching.md).

features.name: Packing plant: building east of the chimney (unidentified)
features.use: unknown - perhaps refrigerator or cooling building
features.evidence: Unlabelled dashed rectangle about 195 ft east of the chimney on the 1957 Tour map. Cow Boy (Dec 1884): main refrigerator building 40x130, corridor about 36x180, passage 18x80.
features.sources: NPS "Tour of Medora" map, Aug 1957 (NMP-TR-7008, in NPSHB 1962 p. 54, 0-600 ft scale); 1956 site plan NMP-TR 3002-A (BROOKS57 Fig. 6); NRHP 75001300; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12-04

features.name: Packing plant: holding pens
features.evidence: Dash-dot enclosure divided into 4-5 pens about 840 ft northeast of the chimney on the 1957 Tour map and 1956 site plan.
features.sources: NPS "Tour of Medora" map, Aug 1957 (NMP-TR-7008, in NPSHB 1962 p. 54, 0-600 ft scale); 1956 site plan NMP-TR 3002-A (BROOKS57 Fig. 6); NRHP 75001300; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12-04

features.name: The Marquis's dam (ice pond)
features.built_text: built May 1884 just below the railroad bridge; rebuilt with flood-gates Oct 1885
features.use: ice harvesting; protected the slaughter house
features.evidence: "below the railroad bridge" (Cow Boy 1884-05-08); the river flows north, so below = just north of the bridge. Huffman's 1886 "Packing House" shows a pond in front of the plant.

features.name: Mrs. Malloy's hotel (Medora)
features.built_text: built on one of Joe Ferris's lots on Main Street; Mrs. Malloy moved in July 15, 1885
features.removed_text: "the Malloy building at Medora" torn down and moved to Dickinson, June 1887
features.evidence: On Main Street on a Ferris lot (Cow Boy 1885-07-16). The 1886 fire warning ran "between Mrs. Malloy's hotel and Bob Roberts' saloon," so it is placed at the other end of the Ferris block.
features.sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-07-16, 1886-03-25, 1886-10; Dickinson Press 1887-06-18
features.notes: Taken over by Arch Boyd Oct 1886.

features.name: John Kiefer's house
features.built_text: built about June 1885 on Third Avenue
features.evidence: Lots 13-14, Block 9, foreclosed 1886 (Cow Boy); house on Third Avenue (Cow Boy 1885-06). Placed on today's Block 9 lots 13-18 parcel.

features.name: Pioneer Hotel, Little Missouri
features.evidence: "close to the depot" (Cow Boy ad, 1884). Placeholder near the depot.

features.name: Tiser House ("only original building of the town of Little Missouri")
features.evidence: "about .1 of a mile west of the Medora bridge" in 1957 (BROOKS57 p. 32). Placed roughly 0.1 mi west of the river on the north side; the 1957 bridge position needs fixing from the 1957-62 aerials.
features.notes: Standing in 1957, occupied by the Ira Tiser family.

features.name: De Mores company office and store (probable), three joined front-gabled buildings; on the site later given to the Medora Stage & Forwarding Co.
features.built_text: photographed winter 1883-84 (Houghton 3013533); standing in the 1885 photos
features.use: NPRC store, post office, meat market and company offices (Cow Boy); probably also the office, warehouse and baggage room of the Medora-Deadwood stage line (NPSHB), Oct 1884-May 1885
features.evidence: Building group "E" of the 1885 bird's-eye view, triangulated from SHSND 00042-00071 and 00042-00195. Triangulated from two or more solved photos; sight lines cross within about 1-3 m, so the position is good to roughly +/-10 m once picking error is allowed for. Three matching front-gabled buildings facing east, on the west side of Main Street.
features.sources: SHSND 00042-00071, 00042-00195; HMdb 88033, 303699; NPSHB p. 58 and the 1957 NPS "Tour of Medora" map (site 3); BROOKS57 pp. 19, 22 and Fig. 8 ; Houghton 3013533; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-05-15, 1885-02-05, 1885-06-25
features.photos: shsnd:00042-00071 (1885 bird's-eye, camera solved); shsnd:00042-00195 (1885-86 overview, camera solved) ; houghton:3013533 (winter 1883-84)
features.notes: Identification is inferred: the 1957 Tour map puts the Medora Stage & Forwarding Co. (described as three buildings - office, warehouse and baggage room) on the small triangular block west of De Mores Memorial Park, which is where this group stands. In 1957 one stood on its original site and two had been moved a few feet (BROOKS57 pp. 19, 22). Location graded C because it rests on this identification. Houghton 3013533 ("Medora in 1883. The office and company store of the Marquis") shows three joined front-gabled frame buildings, the form of group "E". The 1957 Tour map puts the stage company (also "three buildings") on this spot, so the stage line probably used the company buildings. Cow Boy: former carriage-house store room (1884-05-15); plank sidewalk in front of "the Co's stores" (1885-02-05); Howe scales in front of the offices (1885-06-25); NPRC general offices moved here from St. Paul, Oct 1885.

features.name: Early schoolhouse (probable site; later the Congregational "Little White Chapel")
features.built_text: "A new school building has been erected" (Bismarck Weekly Tribune 1885-11-20); classes began in a Cantonment building in July 1884 (HMdb 88020)
features.removed_text: remodelled as the Congregational church; burned Jan 1951 (Billings County Pioneer 1951-02-01)
features.evidence: Historic Medora "Congregational Church" panel (photographed on site by Matt Briney, 2026), quoting the Billings County Pioneer of Feb 1, 1951: the burned church was "originally one of the earliest schoolhouses in that vicinity" and some residents said it was "the first building in the town of Medora"; the site "has served as a school, a post office and an apartment building". Placed at today's Congregational Church; whether this was the 1885 school is not confirmed.
features.sources: Bismarck Weekly Tribune 1885-11-20; HMdb 88020; Billings County Pioneer 1951-02-01 (on the Historic Medora panel)
features.photos: shsnd:00042-00037 ("new schoolhouse", c.1930?)
